From 944edca81e7aea15f83cf9a13a6ab67f711e8abd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tzung-Bi Shih <tzungbi@kernel.org>
Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2025 03:39:00 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] platform/chrome: cros_ec_ishtp: Fix UAF after unbinding
 driver

After unbinding the driver, another kthread `cros_ec_console_log_work`
is still accessing the device, resulting an UAF and crash.

The driver doesn't unregister the EC device in .remove() which should
shutdown sub-devices synchronously.  Fix it.

Fixes: 26a14267aff2 ("platform/chrome: Add ChromeOS EC ISHTP driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20251031033900.3577394-1-tzungbi@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Tzung-Bi Shih <tzungbi@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/platform/chrome/cros_ec_ishtp.c b/drivers/platform/chrome/cros_ec_ishtp.c
index 4e74e702c5a2..3766cef81fe8 100644
--- a/drivers/platform/chrome/cros_ec_ishtp.c
+++ b/drivers/platform/chrome/cros_ec_ishtp.c
@@ -667,6 +667,7 @@ static void cros_ec_ishtp_remove(struct ishtp_cl_device *cl_device)
 
 	cancel_work_sync(&client_data->work_ishtp_reset);
 	cancel_work_sync(&client_data->work_ec_evt);
+	cros_ec_unregister(client_data->ec_dev);
 	cros_ish_deinit(cros_ish_cl);
 	ishtp_put_device(cl_device);
 }
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a use-after-free (UAF) bug in the ChromeOS EC ISHTP driver (`cros_ec_ishtp.c`). The issue occurred after unbinding the driver: a kernel thread (`cros_ec_console_log_work`) could still access the device, leading to a crash.

**Modification in the file:**
- **`drivers/platform/chrome/cros_ec_ishtp.c`** – In the `cros_ec_ishtp_remove()` function, a call to `cros_ec_unregister(client_data->ec_dev)` is added.

**Relationship:**
The UAF happened because the EC device was not unregistered during driver removal. Adding `cros_ec_unregister` ensures that all sub-devices (including those involved in the `cros_ec_console_log_work` kthread) are shut down synchronously before the ISHTP client is deinitialized (`cros_ish_deinit`). This eliminates the race condition where the kthread accessed already-freed resources. The call is placed after cancelling pending work items but before the ISHTP deinit, ensuring proper teardown order.

The driver doesn't unregister the EC device in .remove() which should

Fixes: 26a14267aff2 ("platform/chrome: Add ChromeOS EC ISHTP driver")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20251031033900.3577394-1-tzungbi@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Tzung-Bi Shih <tzungbi@kernel.org>

The driver's remove function lacks a call to cros_ec_unregister() to synchronously shut down sub-devices (including the console log work kthread) before deinitializing the ISHTP client. This allows the kthread to continue accessing freed device memory, causing a use-after-free (UAF) crash after unbinding the driver.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static void cros_ec_ishtp_remove(struct ishtp_cl_device *cl_device)
 {
 	struct ishtp_cl	*cros_ish_cl = ishtp_get_drvdata(cl_device);
 	struct ishtp_cl_data *client_data = ishtp_get_client_data(cros_ish_cl);
 
 	cancel_work_sync(&client_data->work_ishtp_reset);
 	cancel_work_sync(&client_data->work_ec_evt);
+	cros_ec_unregister(client_data->ec_dev);
 	cros_ish_deinit(cros_ish_cl);
 	ishtp_put_device(cl_device);
 }
